key_insight: Disordered metal-oxide photonic glasses can produce four target photovoltaic colors, but oxide choice and facade geometry determine color fidelity and angular stability.
engineering_relevance: Colored building-integrated photovoltaics require coordinated design of the oxide, encapsulant, coating layer count, and viewing geometry rather than relying on disorder for angle-independent color.
method: Coupled Mie scattering, Percus–Yevick structure factors, exact phase functions, and two-flux optical transfer.
Included absorption and refraction at the module front glass.
Mapped survey-defined color targets across four oxides, four encapsulants, two cell technologies, and particle/coating parameters.
evidence_signal: Modeling reached blue, green, gold, and terracotta targets with three-layer coatings at ΔE00 = 0.8–2.5, while predicted daily color drift was ΔE00 = 5–18.
watch_item: Disorder does not guarantee angular stability, and green, gold, and terracotta require blue-band absorption by V2O5 rather than a fully transparent scatterer.
paper_title: Engineering Color and Angular Stability in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics Using Metal-Oxide Photonic Glasses
